Alice K: Brought up constellation-embed-3-small (FP16 -> per-channel INT6) on staging this morning. Quick snapshot of the sanity checks below.

Alice K: Metrics (holdout 50k, mixed-lang, production-like query length distribution):
```
Model: constellation-embed-3-small-int6 (per-channel int6)
Baseline: pegasus-embed-v2-fp16

Recall@1: 0.732 -> 0.701 (-3.1 pp)
Recall@5: 0.873 -> 0.862 (-1.1 pp)
Recall@10: 0.912 -> 0.909 (-0.3 pp)
Silhouette (kmeans, k=50): 0.21 -> 0.16
UMAP cluster purity: 0.78 -> 0.66

Notes: drop is concentrated in short queries (<= 6 tokens) and <50-token longtail is stable.
```

Ben R: Thanks. What was the anchor / holdout split and random seed? any rogue examples?

Alice K: Holdout = 50k queries (10k anchors with 5 near/5 far), seed=42. I manually spot-checked ~200 failure pairs; many are short ambiguous queries (e.g., "setup", "install guide").

Priya S: Can you paste the per-length bucket breakdown? suspected quantization collapse for short contexts.

Alice K: Sure — quick bucketed recall (R@1): short(<=6)=0.615 -> 0.538, mid(7-32)=0.755 -> 0.741, long(>32)=0.812 -> 0.806.

Chao L: Interesting — looks like the low-bit dynamic range hitting small vectors. Did we use per-channel scale + asymmetric zero-point?

Alice K: Yes, per-channel symmetric scales with integer rounding; zero-point forced 0 because we used symmetric quant flow in our toolchain.

Chao L: Can we try per-channel asymmetric (learn zpt) and also a small calibration set restricted to short queries? Might recover the short-query mass.

Thomas M: Also let's check whether k-means seeding or PCA whitening differs between runs; small shifts in normalization can blow up silhouette. Did you run whitened features?

Alice K: Current run used L2 normalize after projection, no explicit PCA whitening. I can add whitening & re-run.

ml-ci: CI: recall_sweep #4392 completed for constellation-embed-3-small-int6. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.local/recall/4392 (log + CSV + embeddings tar).

EvalBot: Quick compare plot attached in artifacts: recall_by_length.png and tsne_short_vs_baseline.png

Ben R: If artifacts are accessible, can someone drop a small sample of failure pairs into the thread? makes triage faster.

Alice K: Dropped 40 failure pairs to the artifact bucket and linked them: https://ci.redwood.local/recall/4392/failures_sample.json

Priya S: Looking at a few — many are near-synonym threshold cases. Could be embedding magnitude compression. Suggest running per-layer ablation: quantize last projection only vs whole encoder.

Chao L: Agreed. Also try per-channel symmetric vs per-tensor asymmetric as an AB test. I can script it tonight: 
```bash
./scripts/eval/recall_sweep.sh --model constellation-embed-3-small --quant int6 --modes per-channel-symm per-tensor-asym --buckets short,mid,long --k 1,5,10
```

Alice K: Nice. Scheduling:
- 3929879200: run per-channel-asym (short-bias calib)
- 3929882800: run last-proj-only int6 ablation
- also scheduling baseline fp16 1k-anchor rerun for parity.

Thomas M: Add a small clustering stability test: run kmeans 10x with different seeds and compute median silhouette. If variance is high -> not stable.

Alice K: Will do.

Priya S: If per-channel-asym recovers >2pp on short queries then we can consider keeping int6 with new calibration. If not, we fallback to per-tensor int8 or keep fp16 for short-query route (routing by length).

Ben R: +1 on length-based routing as a short-term mitigation. Also stamp the issue with a perf impact estimate for hybrid routing.

Alice K: Action items: 1) run per-channel-asymmetric int6 + short-calib, 2) run last-proj-only ablation, 3) run whitened-normalization variant, 4) compute clustering stability (10 seeds), 5) rerun baseline fp16 1k-anchor. I'll post artifacts when each job finishes.

Alice K: TL;DR — Constellation-int6 looks promising overall but short-query recall dropped; next steps are targeted quant configs and routing experiments.

Thomas M: Thanks — ping when the per-channel-asym job completes. :thumbsup:
